mechanism_narrative: Steady increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicate a durable return of commuting and out-of-home routines that raises weekday retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -12.4 to -9.7 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to rise.

mechanism_narrative: When the TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -30.0 percent, transit use becomes sufficient to support non-essential retail trips, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -30.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -35.4 to -30.6 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: After TRANSIT exceeds -30.0 percent, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM signals broader willingness to leave home for both leisure and essentials, which spills over into retail-and-recreation spending and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above -22.0 percent while GROCERY_PHARM stays above +1.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered from -34.7 to -21.4 and GROCERY_PHARM held positive at +1.7
failure_condition: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improve but the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A fall in RESIDENTIAL mobility below +5.0 percent above baseline marks reduced stay-at-home behavior, freeing households for retail trips and driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +5.0 percent
regime_hint: residential mobility declining below 5 percent above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after RESIDENTIAL falls below +5.0 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace reopening policy gains become visible when WORKPLACES crosses above -10.0 percent; this office return increases lunchtime and after-work retail demand, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -10.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -12.1 to -10.9 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: After WORKPLACES exceeds -10.0 percent, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM below +2.0 percent indicates essential-trip demand is saturated, so households reallocate trips to discretionary retail and raise RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean remains below +2.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was +1.0, +1.4, +1.7, +1.7 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM remains below +2.0 percent, RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: Monsoon conditions keep PARKS below -20.0 percent, pushing outdoor leisure trips toward indoor retail and recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean stays below -20.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -34.7, -20.0, -19.0, and -21.4 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than over the last 28 days while PARKS remains below -20.0 percent.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT rising faster than WORKPLACES indicates discretionary travel rather than only commuting; this mix produces shopping and recreation trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.8 points while WORKPLACES improved 1.2 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: When TRANSIT improves faster than WORKPLACES, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its last 28-day mean.
